title: OutcomeBound decision briefs v1
description: The input of `outcomebound brief`: the decision briefs an agent puts to a person, and the order among them. Every brief carries `id`, `heading` and `undo`; any other field may be left out, and a field left out writes no line. The command writes marks only from these fields, and also refuses what this schema cannot say: an option that is not exactly three strings, a pair in `facts` or `order` that is not exactly two, a diagram edge that is not two or three, a string holding a line break, a control or format character or a mark's own glyph, a diagram label holding a double quote or an edge label holding a |, a `facts` label naming a line the renderer writes, a repeated id, and an `order` label that is no brief's id. It refuses with exit 1, naming the brief, a brief with two or more options and no `recommend` or no `recommend_way`, and a brief with none of `checked`, `not_checked` and `facts`. It does not vouch for what the text says: the verdicts under `checked` are the agent's own report of commands it ran, and the passed mark means only that every verdict given is PASS.

briefs.description: The briefs, in the order they are put to the person.

id.description: The id the person answers by, such as D3: a letter followed by letters, digits and hyphens, unique in the document. The renderer joins it to the heading with the separator of the symbols it draws in, and `order` names briefs by it.

recommend.description: Why the recommendation is what it is; required where there are two or more `options`, and written after the recommended Option's letter.

recommend_way.description: The way of `options` that is recommended, spelled as it is there; required where there are two or more, and the renderer writes its letter.

confidence.description: `fact`, or a whole percentage followed by `(inferred)`; written only with `recommend`.

options.description: Every way forward, as exactly three strings, [the way, what it leads to, its downside], which the command checks; the downside is written under its Option behind a mark of its own. The command refuses a single one, since a brief lays out Options only where there are two or more.

checked.description: The verdict of every check the line names, and the line's text; the mark that means a check passed is written only where every verdict is PASS.

not_checked.description: What could not be checked, why, and what would settle it. A brief carries at least one of `checked`, `not_checked` and `facts`.

facts.description: Facts the agent knows that bear on the answer, as [label, text] pairs, each written as its own unmarked line after Not checked; a label may not take the name of a line the renderer writes.

undo.description: Required on every brief: how it is undone, or, with `can_be_undone` false, what cannot be undone.

diagram.description: Drawn after the brief's list where order, dependency, flow or before/after is the point: a Mermaid flowchart where the surface renders Mermaid, and ASCII chains otherwise; every edge is drawn as given, and none is reduced away.

caption.description: The line written above the diagram.

edges.description: Each edge as [from, to] or [from, to, label], in the order they are drawn; no label holds a double quote, and no edge label a |.

order.description: The order among the briefs, as [before, after] pairs: after waits on before.
